paragraphs.text: Congenital myasthenic syndrome-11 is an autosomal recessive disorder of neuromuscular transmission caused by defects in rapsyn, which result in endplate acetylcholine receptor (AChR) deficiency (Ohno et al., 2002). Onset is usually perinatal or in the first years of life. Features include bilateral ptosis, fatigable weakness of facial, bulbar, and limb muscles, and crisis-like exacerbations with respiratory insufficiency provoked by stress, fever, or infection (Muller et al., 2003; Milone et al., 2009). Some patients have arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, and a later-onset form also exists (Burke et al., 2003).

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2003) described 12 European patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome from 10 families, all carrying the RAPSN N88K mutation. Symptoms usually began perinatally or in the first years of life, although 1 patient had no myasthenic symptoms before the third decade. Typical features were bilateral ptosis and weakness of facial, bulbar, and limb muscles. In early childhood, patients had frequent crisis-like exacerbations with respiratory insufficiency provoked by stress, fever, or infections. Myasthenic symptoms were generally mild to moderate, but severity and age at onset varied greatly.

paragraphs.text: Ohno et al. (2003) identified mutations in the RAPSN promoter region in 8 patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome. Patient 1 carried a -27C-G mutation, which changes an E-box at positions -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG. The allele carrying this mutation was not transcribed in the patient's muscle. Patients 2 through 8 were all of Oriental Jewish stock of Iraqi or Iranian origin and carried a -38A-G mutation. This mutation changes an E-box at positions -40 to -35 from CAACTG to CAGCTG without affecting the consensus CANNTG sequence. Haplotype analysis indicated that the -38A-G mutation arose from a common founder. Both mutations attenuated reporter expression in C2C12 myotubes, and they altered binding to C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts in electrophoretic mobility shift assays.
